name: Bahrain
title: Bahrain UTM and Thickness Gauging | ASRY Ship-Repair Yard
description: Bahrain hull gauging at the ASRY ship-repair yard and Khalifa Bin Salman Port: pre-docking estimates, ESP renewal survey and CAP thickness measurement.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement at Bahrain's Ship-Repair Yard and Ports
intro: Bahrain's maritime economy centres on the Arab Shipbuilding and Repair Yard (ASRY) at Hidd, one of the Gulf's main dry-docking yards for tankers, gas carriers and offshore units, with Khalifa Bin Salman Port next door handling the island's container trade. When a ship is booked into ASRY for a renewal survey or major repair, ultrasonic thickness measurement in Bahrain can start before the docking and continue through it, carried out by technicians who travel from India on a plan built around the yard date.

highlights.p: Very large crude carriers due for a third or subsequent renewal survey need extensive ESP gauging throughout the cargo and ballast tanks. We work through the TM plan tank by tank as the yard releases each space.

Gauging at the repair berth or anchorage before docking shows where substantial and excessive corrosion lies. The yard can order steel and plan renewal from the first day in dock instead of halfway through.
Once new plating and stiffeners are fitted, we return to measure the renewed areas, so the owner and the attending class surveyor have a measured record that the repair meets the required thickness.

port.h: Bahrain's ports, terminals and the yard at Hidd
p: Bahrain is a small island state, but its maritime footprint reaches across the central Gulf. Khalifa Bin Salman Port at Hidd, operated by APM Terminals Bahrain, handles the kingdom's container and general cargo trade and took over from the older Mina Salman as the main commercial port. The Bapco refinery at Sitra exports refined products from its own marine terminal, and the King Fahd Causeway links the island by road to Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province, whose ports and oil terminals generate much of the ship traffic in this part of the Gulf.

For inspection, the dominant feature is ASRY. The yard, on the Hidd peninsula and established by member states of OAPEC, has been repairing crude carriers, gas ships, bulkers and offshore units for decades. Its large dry dock can take very large crude carriers, and further docking and repair berths handle smaller ships. Its position in the middle of the Gulf puts it within easy reach of ships trading to the Saudi, Kuwaiti, Qatari and Emirati loading ports, and a renewal-survey docking normally lasts long enough for a full thickness measurement programme, from pre-docking readings to confirmation after repair.

That makes Bahrain's inspection demand docking-led. Pre-docking gauging to estimate steel renewal, full programmes when ESP tankers and bulk carriers come in for renewal survey, CAP gauging in Bahrain for older crude tankers, and confirmation readings after steel renewal all cluster around the yard. Outside ASRY, container ships at Khalifa Bin Salman Port, product tankers at Sitra and the workboats and offshore support craft working in the central Gulf generate smaller scopes. Ships also wait off Bahrain for a docking slot, which gives a window for afloat readings before they enter the yard. Because so much of the work is concentrated in one place, a superintendent can plan gauging, repair and survey as a single sequence rather than across several ports.

facilities.h: Where thickness gauging at ASRY and around Bahrain takes place
p: The bulk of the work is done at the ASRY ship-repair yard, either in dry dock or at the repair berths before and after docking. Thickness measurement at Hidd starts, where possible, before the ship enters dock: readings taken at anchorage or at the repair berth let the superintendent and the yard agree steel quantities early, which protects the docking schedule. In dock, we follow the yard's sequence of tank cleaning, ventilation and staging, report substantial and excessive corrosion as each tank is completed, and return for confirmation readings once new steel is fitted.

Away from the yard, container ships calling at Khalifa Bin Salman Port can have piping, deck and limited tank gauging during longer stays, and product tankers lying idle off Sitra can be gauged at anchorage with launch access through the agent. Tugs, workboats and supply vessels working in Bahraini waters are gauged at their own berths or during their docking periods when their renewal surveys come round. The short distances on the island mean a team at the yard can usually reach a second vessel at the port or an anchorage launch point on the same day.
list: ASRY dry dock — full renewal-survey programmes on VLCCs, Suezmaxes, gas carriers and bulk carriers, including the ESP extent in cargo and ballast tanks
ASRY repair berths — pre-docking gauging and afloat tank readings before the ship enters dock, plus confirmation readings after steel renewal
Khalifa Bin Salman Port — piping, deck and hatch-coaming gauging on container and general cargo ships during port calls, with ISPS passes via the agent
Off Sitra and the refinery terminal — condition gauging on product tankers between cargoes, within the terminal's permit system
Bahrain anchorages — pre-purchase and on-hire gauging on tankers and bulkers lying at anchor ahead of an ASRY slot or awaiting orders
Workboat and offshore craft berths — renewal-survey gauging on tugs, crew boats and offshore support craft working in the central Gulf

context.h: Port state control, ESP surveys and Bahrain's role in the Gulf
p: Bahrain belongs to the Riyadh MoU, and ships calling at its ports are inspected under that regime. Many of the ships docking at ASRY are crude and product tankers or bulk carriers in the ESP category defined by SOLAS chapter XI-1 regulation 2, with the 2011 ESP Code setting the survey programme, so the extent of gauging is set by IACS UR Z10.1, Z10.2, Z10.4 or Z10.5 depending on ship type, and increases markedly from the third renewal survey onwards. Getting the TM plan right before the docking, with compartments, sections and points agreed at the survey planning meeting with the attending surveyor, is one of the biggest factors in keeping the yard schedule.

There is no emission control area in the Gulf, so MARPOL Annex VI's 0.50% global sulphur cap applies, and scrubber-fitted tankers and bulk carriers docking at ASRY can have their wash-water and overboard piping measured while the system is shut down. The central Gulf's climate is hard on ships: shallow, warm and highly saline water, intense summer heat on decks and humid nights accelerate coating breakdown in ballast tanks and corrosion of deck structure. Bahrain's position between Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the UAE, and its road link to the Eastern Province, also make it practical for owners combining a docking with port calls across the region.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Bahrain
jobs.p: An ASRY docking date is where nearly every Bahrain enquiry begins. The scopes below reflect what superintendents commonly request, from pre-docking estimates to post-repair confirmation. Each is built from the ship's previous gauging reports, the survey requirements for its age and type, and the yard's working sequence, so readings arrive while they can still change the repair list and the steel order.
list: A VLCC at ASRY for its third renewal survey: ESP gauging of deck, bottom, side shell, transverse webs and longitudinals in cargo and ballast tanks, with daily reporting to the superintendent.
Pre-docking gauging of a Suezmax at the ASRY repair berth or anchorage, so steel renewal quantities are agreed with the yard before the dock date.
Confirmation readings after steel renewal in the ballast tanks of a bulk carrier, giving the owner and class surveyor a measured record that renewed areas meet the required thickness.

Wall-thickness checks on the exhaust gas cleaning system of a Capesize bulk carrier shut down in dock: wash-water supply, discharge and overboard lines, shell penetrations and the bends downstream of the pumps.
Ship inspection in Bahrain for a prospective buyer: condition gauging of a product tanker at anchorage, sampling deck, ballast tanks and cargo-tank structure.

logistics: Technicians arrive at Bahrain International Airport (BAH) on Muharraq, which is served directly from several Indian cities and lies close to Hidd; King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, reached over the causeway, is an alternative when the team is coming from a job in Saudi Arabia. The owner's site team sets up yard access at ASRY, Khalifa Bin Salman Port requires ISPS passes arranged by the agent, and anchorage work needs a launch. Bahraini visas are sorted out before the team travels, which is why we like to confirm the job the moment the docking slot is booked.

faqs.q: Is it worth gauging before the ship goes into dock at ASRY?
faqs.a: Yes, and we recommend it. Pre-docking readings taken at anchorage or at the repair berth identify the tanks and areas with substantial or excessive corrosion ahead of docking, which lets the yard order steel and plan renewal from day one. Without them, steel quantities are often estimated in dock, which tends to stretch the docking period.

faqs.q: What information do you need for an ESP renewal survey at ASRY?
faqs.a: The ship's structural drawings, the previous thickness measurement reports, the class survey status and any outstanding conditions of class, and the planned docking dates. With these we prepare a draft TM plan by compartment and section, which the superintendent takes to the survey planning meeting with the attending class surveyor. Earlier corrosion trends tell us where wastage was already approaching the substantial-corrosion threshold.

faqs.q: Can CAP gauging be done during an ASRY docking?
faqs.a: It often is, because the ship is gas-free, staged and accessible. CAP is a voluntary class programme, run separately by each classification society, and charterers ask for it on older tankers, typically from about 15 years. Combining the CAP readings with the renewal-survey programme avoids gauging the same structure twice; we agree the combined scope with the superintendent and the class society before the ship docks.

faqs.q: How does the central Gulf climate affect ballast tanks on ships docking at ASRY?
faqs.a: Ships trading in the central Gulf carry warm, highly saline ballast and spend months with sun-heated decks. Coatings in upper wing tanks and under-deck areas break down faster, and once the coating goes, pitting and general wastage follow quickly. We pay particular attention to deck longitudinals inside ballast tanks, upper stools on bulk carriers, and the areas around bellmouths and ladders, where early losses are commonly found.
